name: Tidal Mudflat
desc: A vast tidal flat at the bottom of the light — dendritic drainage creeks branch across ribbed silt toward a low horizon, pans of standing water hold the shivering sky, and the tide line creeps in and out over minutes under a sun that never quite clears the haze; low-light large-format, an albumen plate, a silver nocturne, SAR radar backscatter, or a bare survey chart.

energy.doc: how hard the water works — pan shimmer, specular streaks, tide-line brightness and the low sun's burn

scale.doc: feature size of the flat — ripple amplitude, creek width, pan size (rebuilds the ground)

density.doc: creek count, number of standing pans, and how many waders work the flat

speed.doc: cloud drift rate across the sky strata

tide.doc: where the water's edge sits — 0 is a drained flat at the horizon, 1 is water at your feet

haze.doc: aerial perspective — horizon value-compression and the printed vignette

hue.doc: palette hue shift off the default cold-sky/warm-band pairing

x.doc: where the low sun sits along the horizon

y.doc: horizon height — low y gives the big-sky read

style.doc: aesthetic: lowlight = cold large-format photograph with one warm band; sepia = warm albumen plate, heavy grain; nocturne = silver moonlit dark key; radar = SAR backscatter false-colour, water reads as black void; contour = drafting-blue survey chart, pure line, no tonal mass

act.doc: multi-minute tide programme indexed off the section arc

seed.doc: regenerates the creek network, ripples and grain

alpha.doc: how far the world sits back behind the performers
